focus: Exodus 19 brings Israel to the Wilderness of Sinai, where the LORD reminds them that He bore them on eagles’ wings and brought them to Himself, and calls them to be His special treasure, a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation. The people agree to do all He has spoken and consecrate themselves for two days, and on the third day they meet God at the foot of a mountain wrapped in fire, smoke, and the sound of the trumpet, with boundaries that guard His holiness.

sections.title: Israel Arrives and Camps Before the Mountain
sections.summary: In the third month after leaving Egypt, Israel comes from Rephidim to the Wilderness of Sinai. “Israel camped there before the mountain” (Exodus 19:2).

sections.title: The LORD Calls Israel to Be His Treasured Kingdom of Priests
sections.summary: From the mountain the LORD tells Moses to remind Israel, “I bore you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself” (Exodus 19:4), and promises that if they obey His voice and keep His covenant, they will be His special treasure, “a kingdom of priests and a holy nation” (Exodus 19:6). The people answer together, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do” (Exodus 19:8), and Moses brings their words back to the LORD.

sections.title: The People Prepare to Meet God on the Third Day
sections.summary: The LORD says He will come in a thick cloud so the people can hear Him speak with Moses, and He commands them to consecrate themselves and wash their clothes today and tomorrow and be ready for the third day. Moses sets bounds around the mountain that no one may touch, and the people prepare.

sections.title: The LORD Descends on Sinai in Fire
sections.summary: On the third day thunder, lightning, a thick cloud, and a very loud trumpet fill the mountain, and the people tremble as Moses brings them out to meet God. Mount Sinai smokes like a furnace and quakes, “because the LORD descended upon it in fire” (Exodus 19:18), and God answers Moses by voice.

sections.title: Moses Is Sent to Warn the People Not to Break Through
sections.summary: The LORD calls Moses to the top of the mountain and sends him back down to warn the people and the priests not to break through to gaze at the LORD, lest He break out against them. Moses goes down with the command to come up again with Aaron, and he speaks to the people.

1.brief: In the third month after leaving Egypt, on the same day, Israel comes to the Wilderness of Sinai. The people arrive at the mountain where God promised Moses they would serve Him.
1.explain:
“In the third month after the children of Israel had gone out of the land of Egypt,”

Israel arrives at Sinai “in the third month” after leaving Egypt. About seven weeks have passed since the Passover.

“on the same day, they came to the Wilderness of Sinai.”

The phrase “on the same day” probably means on the first day of that month, the new moon. The people have reached the place God promised Moses at the burning bush: “you shall serve God on this mountain” (3:12).
1.notes:
Later Jewish tradition linked the giving of the law with the Feast of Weeks (Pentecost), fifty days after Passover. Scripture itself does not make that link.

The exact location of Mount Sinai is debated. The traditional site is Jebel Musa in the southern Sinai Peninsula. Other locations have been proposed in northern Sinai and in Arabia (compare Galatians 4:25).

2.brief: Having departed from Rephidim, Israel camps in the wilderness, “before the mountain.” The whole people now stand at the place of meeting with God.
2.explain:
“For they had departed from Rephidim, had come to the Wilderness of Sinai, and camped in the wilderness.”

The verse traces the last stage of the journey, from “Rephidim” (17:1) to “the Wilderness of Sinai.”

“So Israel camped there before the mountain.”

Israel camps “before the mountain.” The whole people now stand at the place of meeting with God. They will stay here for nearly a year (Numbers 10:11).

3.brief: Moses goes up to God, and the LORD calls to him from the mountain with a message for the house of Jacob. God initiates the meeting and speaks through Moses to His people.
3.explain:
“And Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain, saying,”

Moses “went up to God,” and “the LORD called to him.” God initiates the meeting and speaks to Moses from the mountain.

“Thus you shall say to the house of Jacob, and tell the children of Israel:”

The message is for the whole people. God calls them “the house of Jacob” and “the children of Israel,” reminding them of their father, whom God renamed Israel.

4.brief: God says, “You have seen what I did to the Egyptians, and how I bore you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself.” The goal of the exodus is not only freedom but a people brought to God Himself.
4.explain:
“You have seen what I did to the Egyptians,”

God begins with what He has done. Israel had “seen” the plagues and the sea with their own eyes. God’s call to obedience rests on His completed rescue.

“and how I bore you on eagles’ wings and brought you to Myself.”

God pictures the journey as being carried “on eagles’ wings.” He carried them as a great bird carries its young, strong, swift, and safe. The goal was not just escape. God “brought you to Myself.” The exodus led Israel into relationship with God.
4.notes: Deuteronomy 32:11–12 develops the picture of an eagle stirring up its nest, spreading its wings, and carrying its young. The bird may be an eagle or a vulture, since the Hebrew word covers both.

5.brief: If they obey His voice and keep His covenant, they will be “a special treasure to Me above all people; for all the earth is Mine.” The God who owns all the earth chooses Israel as His own treasured people.
5.explain:
“Now therefore, if you will indeed obey My voice and keep My covenant,”

“Now therefore” links the call to obey with what God has done. Israel is to “obey My voice and keep My covenant.” Obedience is the response of a rescued people, not the price of their rescue.

“then you shall be a special treasure to Me above all people;”

Israel will be God’s “special treasure.” The word was used for a king’s personal treasure, his own valued possession. Among all nations, Israel will belong to God in a special way.

“for all the earth is Mine.”

God owns “all the earth.” He did not choose Israel because He lacked other peoples. The God who owns all the earth chooses Israel as His own treasured people.
5.notes: The Hebrew word for “special treasure” is segullah. It appears also in Deuteronomy 7:6; 14:2; 26:18, and in Malachi 3:17.

6.brief: Israel will be to Him “a kingdom of priests and a holy nation,” and Moses is to speak these words to the people. Israel is called to a priestly and holy role among the nations, a calling 1 Peter 2:9 applies to the church.
6.explain:
“And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.”

Israel will be “a kingdom of priests.” A priest stood between God and others, bringing them near to God. Israel was to serve that role among the nations. They would also be “a holy nation,” set apart for God and different from the peoples around them. Israel is called to a priestly and holy role among the nations.

“These are the words which you shall speak to the children of Israel.”

Moses is to carry these words to the people exactly. Peter applies these titles to the people who belong to Christ: “But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people” (1 Peter 2:9). He adds that those who once were not a people are now the people of God (1 Peter 2:10).

7.brief: Moses calls the elders and lays before them all the words the LORD commanded. God’s offer is placed before the people’s leaders.
7.explain:
“So Moses came and called for the elders of the people,”

Moses comes down and gathers “the elders,” the leaders of the people.

“and laid before them all these words which the LORD commanded him.”

Moses sets God’s words before them. God’s offer is placed before the people’s leaders.

8.brief: All the people answer together, “All that the LORD has spoken we will do,” and Moses reports their words to the LORD. Israel responds as one to God’s call.
8.explain:
“Then all the people answered together and said, ‘All that the LORD has spoken we will do.”

The people respond with one voice. “All that the LORD has spoken we will do.” Israel responds as one to God’s call. They will repeat these words twice more when the covenant is confirmed (24:3, 7).

“So Moses brought back the words of the people to the LORD.”

Moses reports the people’s answer to God. He acts as the go-between.
8.notes: Israel’s promise was soon broken at the golden calf (32:1–8).

9.brief: The LORD says He will come in a thick cloud so that the people may hear when He speaks with Moses and believe him forever. God will confirm Moses as His spokesman before the whole people.
9.explain:
“And the LORD said to Moses, ‘Behold, I come to you in the thick cloud,”

God will come “in the thick cloud.” The cloud both reveals and hides Him. The people will know He is there, but they will not see Him.

“that the people may hear when I speak with you, and believe you forever.”

God’s purpose is that the people “may hear” Him speak with Moses and “believe you forever.” God will confirm Moses as His spokesman before the whole people.

“So Moses told the words of the people to the LORD.”

The narrator repeats that Moses reported the people’s words (19:8).

10.brief: The LORD tells Moses to consecrate the people today and tomorrow and have them wash their clothes. Meeting the holy God requires preparation.
10.explain:
“Then the LORD said to Moses, ‘Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow,”

Moses is to “consecrate” the people over two days. Meeting the holy God requires preparation.

“and let them wash their clothes.”

Washing their clothes was an outward sign of inner readiness. They were to come before God clean.

11.brief: The people must be ready for the third day, when the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all. God’s coming will be public and visible.
11.explain:
“And let them be ready for the third day.”

The people must be “ready” for the day God will come.

“For on the third day the LORD will come down upon Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.”

God Himself will descend, and every Israelite will see it. God’s coming will be public and visible.

12.brief: Moses is to set bounds around the mountain, and anyone who touches it shall surely be put to death. The boundaries guard the people from the danger of approaching God’s holiness carelessly.
12.explain:
“You shall set bounds for the people all around, saying,”

Moses is to “set bounds,” marking a boundary line around the mountain.

“Take heed to yourselves that you do not go up to the mountain or touch its base.”

The people may not climb the mountain or even “touch its base.” The mountain will be holy because God is there.

“Whoever touches the mountain shall surely be put to death.”

The penalty for crossing the line is death. The boundaries guard the people from the danger of approaching God’s holiness carelessly.

13.brief: No one is to touch the offender, who must be stoned or shot, man or beast, and when the trumpet sounds long they may come near the mountain. The holiness of the place is enforced strictly until God signals the time to approach.
13.explain:
“Not a hand shall touch him, but he shall surely be stoned or shot with an arrow;”

No one is to touch the person who crosses the line. He is to be put to death from a distance, by stones or arrows. Even touching the offender would mean crossing the boundary.

“whether man or beast, he shall not live.”

The rule applies to animals as well as people.

“When the trumpet sounds long, they shall come near the mountain.”

When “the trumpet sounds long,” the people may “come near.” God Himself will signal when they may approach. The holiness of the place is enforced strictly until God gives the signal.
13.notes: The Hebrew word for “trumpet” here is yobel, a ram’s horn. The same word gives its name to the Year of Jubilee (Leviticus 25:10).

14.brief: Moses goes down, sanctifies the people, and they wash their clothes. Israel obeys God’s instructions for preparation.
14.explain:
“So Moses went down from the mountain to the people and sanctified the people, and they washed their clothes.”

Moses obeys, and so do the people. They are “sanctified,” set apart, and they wash their clothes. Israel obeys God’s instructions for preparation.

15.brief: Moses tells the people to be ready for the third day and not to come near their wives. Their whole lives are to be set apart in readiness to meet God.
15.explain:
“And he said to the people, ‘Be ready for the third day;”

Moses repeats God’s instruction to be ready.

“do not come near your wives.”

Moses adds that husbands are to abstain from sexual relations during these days. This was not because marriage was unclean but because the people were to give themselves wholly to preparing to meet God (compare 1 Corinthians 7:5). Their whole lives are to be set apart in readiness to meet God.
15.notes: Leviticus 15:18 treats marital relations as making a person ceremonially unclean until evening, which may explain the instruction here.

16.brief: On the morning of the third day there are thunder, lightning, a thick cloud, and a very loud trumpet, and all the people tremble. God’s coming is overwhelming and awe-inspiring.
16.explain:
“Then it came to pass on the third day, in the morning, that there were thunderings and lightnings, and a thick cloud on the mountain;”

On the third day God comes as He promised. There are “thunderings and lightnings” and “a thick cloud.”

“and the sound of the trumpet was very loud, so that all the people who were in the camp trembled.”

“The sound of the trumpet” grows “very loud.” No human trumpeter is mentioned. The whole camp trembles. God’s coming is overwhelming and awe-inspiring.

17.brief: Moses brings the people out of the camp to meet with God, and they stand at the foot of the mountain. The people come as close as God permits.
17.explain:
“to meet with God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.”

Moses leads the people out of the camp “to meet with God.” They stand “at the foot of the mountain,” as close as the boundary allows. The people come as close as God permits.
17.notes: Deuteronomy 4:10–12 recalls this day as the day Israel “stood before the LORD your God in Horeb,” when they heard His voice but saw no form.

18.brief: Mount Sinai is covered in smoke “because the LORD descended upon it in fire,” and the whole mountain quakes. The LORD Himself has come down in holy power.
18.explain:
“Now Mount Sinai was completely in smoke, because the LORD descended upon it in fire.”

The mountain is wrapped “in smoke.” The reason is that “the LORD descended upon it in fire.” Fire is a frequent sign of God’s holy presence, as at the burning bush (3:2).

“Its smoke ascended like the smoke of a furnace, and the whole mountain quaked greatly.”

The mountain looks like a kiln and shakes beneath God’s presence. The LORD Himself has come down in holy power. Hebrews later contrasts this scene with believers’ approach to God through Jesus, the Mediator of the new covenant (Hebrews 12:22–24), while still calling them to serve God “with reverence and godly fear. For our God is a consuming fire” (Hebrews 12:28–29).
18.notes: Hebrews 12:18–21 recalls this scene: the fire, the darkness, the trumpet, and the voice so terrifying that even Moses said, “I am exceedingly afraid and trembling.”

19.brief: As the trumpet grows louder and louder, Moses speaks, and God answers him by voice. God speaks openly with Moses before the people.
19.explain:
“And when the blast of the trumpet sounded long and became louder and louder,”

The trumpet grows “louder and louder.”

“Moses spoke, and God answered him by voice.”

The phrase translated by voice may also be read with thunder. God speaks openly with Moses before the people, as He promised in 19:9.

20.brief: The LORD comes down on the top of Mount Sinai and calls Moses to the top, and Moses goes up. Moses alone is called into God’s nearer presence.
20.explain:
“Then the LORD came down upon Mount Sinai, on the top of the mountain.”

The narrator again stresses that “the LORD came down.” He meets His people on “the top of the mountain.”

“And the LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.”

God calls Moses up to Himself. Moses alone is called into God’s nearer presence.

21.brief: The LORD tells Moses to go down and warn the people not to break through to gaze at the LORD, lest many perish. God protects the people from the danger of His holiness.
21.explain:
“And the LORD said to Moses, ‘Go down and warn the people,”

As soon as Moses arrives, God sends him back down with a warning.

“lest they break through to gaze at the LORD, and many of them perish.”

The danger is that the people will “break through” the boundary out of curiosity “to gaze at the LORD.” If they do, “many of them” will die. God protects the people from the danger of His holiness.

22.brief: The priests who come near the LORD must also consecrate themselves, lest the LORD break out against them. Even those who serve before God must approach Him with care.
22.explain:
“Also let the priests who come near the LORD consecrate themselves,”

“The priests” must also “consecrate themselves.” Aaron and his sons had not yet been appointed (28:1). The text does not say who these priests were. They may have been those who served in that role before the law, such as heads of families.

“lest the LORD break out against them.”

If they come carelessly, “the LORD” will “break out against them,” like a sudden breach in a wall. Even those who serve before God must approach Him with care.

23.brief: Moses answers that the people cannot come up, because God already warned them to set bounds around the mountain. Moses believes the warning has already been obeyed.
23.explain:
“But Moses said to the LORD, ‘The people cannot come up to Mount Sinai;”

Moses thinks the warning is unnecessary. “The people cannot come up.”

“for You warned us, saying, ‘Set bounds around the mountain and consecrate it.”

Moses reminds God that the bounds are already set. Moses believes the warning has already been obeyed.

24.brief: The LORD tells Moses to go down and come back up with Aaron, but the priests and people must not break through. God repeats the warning because the danger is real.
24.explain:
“Then the LORD said to him, ‘Away! Get down and then come up, you and Aaron with you.”

God insists. “Away! Get down.” Moses is to go down and come back up with “Aaron.”

“But do not let the priests and the people break through to come up to the LORD, lest He break out against them.”

God repeats the warning. The priests and people must not cross the line. God repeats the warning because the danger is real.

25.brief: Moses goes down to the people and speaks to them. Moses carries God’s warning to the people just before God speaks His commandments.
25.explain:
“So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.”

Moses obeys. He goes down and delivers God’s warning. Moses carries the warning to the people just before God speaks His commandments.
